messages:
Maya (SE): starting POC thread for NorthStar Finance — they need streaming chat with server-initiated tool calls into their transaction service, strict JSON schema enforcement, and examples in Go. Main asks: ephemeral creds pattern, token rotation cadence, pricing variants (hosted vs reserved), and SOC2/KMS language.
Colin (AE): customer expects ~200 rps peak during batch windows, avg response ~120 tokens. Their procurement wants to see a reserved vs hosted cost comparison and whether dedicated is required for p95 < 250ms.
Diego (Eng): for 200 rps and ~120 tokens we usually recommend a 1-node Dedicated pool for stable p95. Hosted can do pilot but tails vary. Can you confirm hours/day?
Maya (SE): likely 8-10h/day initial pilot. They also want tool calls to be authenticated and for us to rotate any webhook credentials automatically.
Priya (Security): for callbacks we recommend mTLS + IP allowlist + an ephemeral webhook signing token rotated by Redwood. For API calls use short-lived STS tokens (default TTL 15m). Need to know if customer requires customer-managed KMS.
Diego (Eng): Private supports customer KMS/HSM. Dedicated can include EKM addendum in contract; Hosted uses Redwood KMS.
Colin (AE): procurement will push for EKM wording if they host keys. Put that in the questionnaire.
Maya (SE): can you drop a small onboarding runbook and a Go SDK streaming snippet showing handling of tool calls and token refresh?
Diego (Eng): runbook highlights: 1) Provision Dedicated pool (if chosen), 2) Configure model variant + structured_output_mode with strict_schema=true, 3) Set up KV prefix caching, 4) Deploy credential-broker for STS tokens, 5) Provision webhook with mTLS + allowlist, 6) Configure schema_violation webhook.
Diego (Eng): Go SDK streaming example (compact):
```go
ctx := context.Background()
client := redwood.NewClient(redwood.WithTokenProvider(myTokenProvider))
stream, err := client.ChatStream(ctx, "northstar-prod-1", redwood.ChatOptions{Streaming:true, Tools:[]redwood.Tool{txTool}})
if err!=nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for ev := range stream.Events() {
  switch ev.Type {
  case redwood.EventTypeDelta:
    fmt.Print(ev.Delta.Text)
  case redwood.EventTypeToolCall:
    // Handle toolcall request payload (JSON)
    go handleTxTool(ev.ToolRequest)
  case redwood.EventTypeDone:
    log.Println("done")
  }
}
```
Maya (SE): token rotation: how should TokenProvider work for server-to-server services (they don't want long-lived creds on their order service)?
Diego (Eng): pattern: 1) Redwood STS issues short-lived API tokens TTL=15m; 2) Customer runs credential-broker (lambda/container) that exchanges their long-lived service credential for STS token; 3) TokenProvider refreshes when TTL<60s. We can provide a sample Lambda and Terraform for AWS/GCP.
DocsBot: sample STS broker + terraform: https://internal.redwood/poctemplates/northstar-finance (demo artifacts, runbook, sample broker).
Priya (Security): security answers: SOC2 Type II status: standard boilerplate available. KMS: Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM; Dedicated supports addendum for EKM. Webhooks: require mTLS, IP allowlist, minimum TLS1.2, and recommend routing callbacks through customer-owned queue for extra isolation.
Colin (AE): pricing: need two items: hosted per-token pilot estimate and reserved 1-node monthly commit. Can we get ballpark numbers for the 8-10h/day pilot by EOD?
Diego (Eng): rough calc outline: tokens = rps * avg_tokens * seconds_per_day * days. For 200 rps, 120 tokens, 9h/day => ~7.78B tokens/month (30d). Hosted = $X per 1M tokens; reserved = monthly node price + lower unit. I'll draft two scenarios (8h/day pilot and 24/7).
Maya (SE): schema enforcement: customer wants fail-fast on invalid JSON. Can Redwood reject and return clear error codes?
Diego (Eng): yes - enable strict_schema=true with policy action=reject. Service returns 422 + validation details, emits schema_violation events, and can route the raw output to a review queue. Also support auto-fallback to a conservative model if violations spike.
Colin (AE): blockers: 1) legal: EKM wording/contract addendum, 2) need sample credential-broker and Terraform, 3) pricing by EOD, 4) tech kickoff meeting scheduling.
Maya (SE): next steps: 1) Colin confirm pilot hours & legal POC, 2) Diego to post back-of-envelope reserved quote + runbook + sample broker + schema example, 3) Priya to add SOC2/KMS + webhook guidance in questionnaire, 4) schedule 30m tech kickoff for Tue.
Priya (Security): I'll post the questionnaire answers and webhook hardening text within 2 hours.
Diego (Eng): will produce the pilot/reserved numbers and the 1-node tuning checklist in ~3 hours.
Colin (AE): I'll confirm pilot hours from the customer by 4pm PT and update the thread.
Maya (SE): thanks team :thumbsup: tagging @Diego @Priya @DocsBot for deliverables.
